correctness.rationale: Klein-model geodesic-to-line-segment reduction yields exact tangent angular criterion, and independent uniform angles convert the two-point event to an expectation of arccos(tanh a/tanh R). The hyperbolic area density is sinh r/(cosh b-cosh a), and elementary integration by parts plus u=sqrt(cosh^2 r-cosh^2 a) gives the stated explicit formula. Strict monotonicity is by first-order stochastic dominance, with rigorously bounded thin-annulus Taylor errors and bounded convergence for the positive infinite-radius limit. Independent hyperboloid geometry, quadrature and limit simulations pass in the standalone checker; analytic proof, not simulation, covers all real parameters.

value.rationale: The exact finite-annulus visibility law solves a natural nonconvex hyperbolic geometry statistic. Its strict radial ordering and sharp thin-annulus coefficient are structural. In negative curvature the positive limiting probability 2 asin(tanh a)/pi persists as outer radius grows without bound, sharply contrasting with the Euclidean vanishing law; this distinguishes curvature in an elementary and reproducible observable. Restricted scope and historical-priority uncertainty are explicit.
